title: Use Your Own Frontend — SpiderPublish as a headless CMS
summary: Render SpiderPublish content in a frontend you build yourself (Next.js / React on your own Cloudflare Worker, Vercel, or anywhere). Read published content with X-Content-Domain, render article bodies from body_html (escaped, links checked), and use @spideriq/publish-sdk@0.1.0 from npm.spideriq.ai (add '@spideriq:registry=https://npm.spideriq.ai' to .npmrc): createSpiderPublish({ site }), posts/docs/press/changelog/pages/collections readers (get returns null when missing, a wrong site throws SITE_NOT_FOUND), <PostBody> with component mapping, nextCache() tags. Browser code on a verified domain may read only; writes go through your own server route. Use whenever the user asks for 'a headless CMS', 'SpiderPublish behind my Next.js site', 'show my SpiderPublish blog on my own site', or 'render the docs in my React app'.
